newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ RETAIL ENVIRONMENT TOUGHEST IN 40 YRS - HILL.
newsitem.headline: NZ RETAIL ENVIRONMENT TOUGHEST IN 40 YRS - HILL.

text.p: Michael Hill International Ltd (MHI) experienced its toughest trading environment in 40 years in the June year, chairman Michael Hill said on Tuesday.
The Australasian jewellery maker and retailer earlier reported an annual net profit of NZ$5.15 million, down from $5.32 million a year earlier.
That compared with market forecasts of NZ$5.2 million and the company's own stated projection of $5.3-5.5 million.

"Considering I've been in retail jewellery for 40 years, I've got to say this is the toughest, most hostile trading environment we've ever experienced," Hill told a briefing of analysts and journalists. "Overall, it was a diabolical year."
Hill said the company had come through strongly with its emphasis on training and a stronger manufacturing base.
"If you follow other retailers, particularly in Australia, we are really swimming against the current, against the trend," he said.
MHI aimed for continued profitable growth but Hill declined to make projections before the important December season.
Rentals paid in shopping malls have long been a thorn in MHI's side and the company's entry to Victoria had been slow because of the high cost of space there.
Mike Parcell, MHI's managing director for Australia, said U.S. trends were pointing towards retailers moving from malls to free-standing shops but that was yet to be seen in Australia.
New Zealand managing director, Howard Bretherton, said MHI was yet to have talks with St Lukes new manager, Australian shopping mall giant Westfield Holdings.
"We believe their rent demands are unreasonable and we understand, in Australia, their modis. We will argue every case as well as we can," Bretherton said.
MHI twice missed its sales targets, once in December and again in April.
Bretherton said "the die was cast" in December when the company failed to hit the spot with its offer of free phone cards for every minimum purchase.
MHI, best known for its low-cost jewellery, would continue to move upmarket.
"Our image is changing to being a respected jeweller where you would want to make a serious first choice, such as a diamond ring," Hill said.
On the manufacturing side, the company aimed to bring quality back to the kind not seen since early this century.
